1. Heard Mr. M. G. Bhangade, learned senior Advocate for the applicant and Mr. M.J.Khan, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the non-applicants.

2. By this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the applicant is challenging the first information report dated 05.09.2020 bearing Crime No. 325/2020, registered with Police Station, Imamwada, Nagpur.
3. After hearing the learned senior Advocate Mr. M.G. Bhangade qua Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code, prima facie, a case is made out for issuance of notice.
Hence, notice is given to the non-applicants only in respect of the offence punishable under Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code.
Mr. M.J. Khan, learned Additional Public Prosecutor waives service for both the non-applicants.
Mr. Bhangade, learned senior Advocate for the applicant strenuously urged before us for grant of interim relief.

The interim relief which is prayed before this Court orally is that non-applicant no.1 - Police Station Officer, Imamwada, Nagpur shall not take any coercive steps against the applicant or in other words, the applicant should not be arrested for the offence punishable under Section 328 of Ankush S/O Shivnarayan Jaiswal vs State Of Mah. The state of Maharashtra and others in Criminal Appeal No. 742 of 2020 ; Imtiyaz Ahmad .vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others, reported in (2012) 2 SCC 688 and also in the case of Amish Devgan .vs. Union of India and others in Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 160 of 2020.

sentences.text: He submitted that personal liberty of the applicant is most important and as observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Arnab Goswami's case, the personal liberty is the basic fabric of the Constitution of India.
He, therefore, submitted that the interim order in the nature of not taking coercive steps and/or not to arrest the applicant, be granted.

He also prayed for grant of stay to the further investigation by the investigating agency, as contained in prayer clause (ii).
5.
The learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. M. J. Khan strongly opposed the prayer of interim relief.
In order to oppose the interim relief, he relied upon various reported decisions.
He prayed that since the earlier application for pre- arrest bail filed on behalf of the applicant is already rejected 3 141220apl800.20.odt by this Court, the prayer is untenable.

6. For considering the interim relief, we have given our anxious and thoughtful consideration to the facts as well as the decisions those were placed before us in respect of the respective submissions.
7. In Arnab Goswami's case (supra), the petitioner before the Hon'ble Apex Court was arrested for the offence punishable under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code.
The arrest was initially challenged at the Principal Seat of this Court and also it was prayed in the petition that he be released on interim bail.
The said was rejected and against that, an appeal was preferred before the Hon'ble Apex Court.

The Hon'ble Apex Court found that the High Court ought to have granted the interim bail and after taking the survey of various provisions in the Constitution framework,
released the appellant on bail.

8. In Imtiyaz Ahmad's case (supra), the question that was posed before the Hon'ble Apex Court was regarding stay orders being granted to the investigation, FIR or trial in criminal proceedings and thereafter the matter remaining pending for years together.

In such a situation, the Hon'ble Apex Court, in paragraph 55 of the said judgment observed that the power to grant stay of investigation and trial is very extraordinary power given to the High Courts and the same power is to be exercised sparingly only to prevent an abuse of the process and to promote the ends of justice.

It was also 4 141220apl800.20.odt directed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the High Court should make it a point of finally disposing of such proceedings as early as possible but preferably within six months from the date the stay order is issued.
9. In Amish Devgan's case (supra) also, the Hon'ble Apex Court granted interim relief in favour of the petitioner before it.

In this case, the petitioner directly invoked the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble Apex Court under Article 32 of the Constitution of India and while exercising jurisdiction under Article 32, the Hon'ble Apex Court found that the petitioner therein had made out a case and therefore, he was granted interim relief.

sentences.text: In our view Imtiyaz Ahmed's case is not helpful to the applicant inasmuch as the question that was before the Hon'ble Apex Court was altogether different than the interim relief, which the applicant is praying in this case.
In Arnab Goswami's case, the applicant was arrested for the offence punishable under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code.

In paragraph 55, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under :
"55.
Now in this backdrop, it becomes necessary to advert briefly to the contents of the FIR in the present case.
The FIR recites that the spouse of the informant had a company carrying on the business of architecture, interior design and engineering consultancy.
According to the informant, her husband was over the previous two years "having pressure as he did not receive the money of work carried out by him".
The FIR recites that the deceased had called at the office 5 141220apl800.20.odt of the appellant and spoken to his accountant for the payment of money.

Apart from the above statements, it has been stated that the deceased left behind a suicide note stating that his "money is stuck and following owners of respective companies are not paying out legitimate dues".
Prima facie, on the application of the test which has been laid down by this Court in a consistent line of authority which has been noted above, it cannot be said that the appellant was guilty of having abetted the suicide within the meaning of Section 306 of the IPC.

These observations, we must note,
are prima facie at this stage since the High Court is still to take up the petition for quashing.

Clearly however, the High Court in failing to notice the contents of the FIR and to make a prima facie evaluation abdicated its role, functions and jurisdiction when seized of a petition under Section 482 of the CrPC.
The High Court recited the legal position that the jurisdiction to quash under Section 482 has to be exercised sparingly.
These words, however, are not meaningless incantations, but have to be assessed with reference to the contents of the particular FIR before the High Court.
If the High Court were to carry out a prima facie evaluation, it would have been impossible for it not to notice the disconnect between the FIR and the provisions of Section 306 of the IPC.
The failure of the High Court to do so has led it to adopting a position where it left the appellant to pursue his remedies for regular bail under Section 439.
The High Court was clearly in error in failing to perform a duty which is entrusted to it while evaluating a petition under Section 482 albeit at the interim stage."
Thereafter, it was observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the High Court did not consider whether prima facie the ingredients of the offence have been made out or not in the FIR.

11. Learned senior Advocate Mr. Bhangade also referred the order passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Criminal Appeal No. 1006 of 2019 in the case of Kamlesh and another .vs. State of Rajasthan and another.

12. Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code reads as under :-
"Section 328 - Causing hurt by means of poison etc. with intent to commit an offence - Whoever administers to or causes to be taken by any person any poison or any stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug, or other thing with intent to cause hurt to such person, or with intent to commit or to facilitate the commission of an offence or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years,
and shall also be liable to fine."

Before us it was not disputed by the learned senior Advocate that in the State of Maharashtra,
the possession, stocking and sell of scented tobacco "Gutkha" in various forms is not only prohibited but also constitute an offence.
According to the learned senior Advocate, Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code is not at all applicable.

14. On 04.09.2020, on the information received by non- applicant no.2 - Food Safety Officer,
Nagpur, he took search of the business establishment of the applicant and during search, total 1970.80 Kgs of scented tobacco worth Rs.20,10,670/-, and pan masala, which is also prohibited in the State of Maharashtra, was seized.

After the seizure, a crime was registered at Police Station,
Imamwada, Nagpur vide Crime No. 325/2020 for the offence punishable under Sections 26, 27 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code.

15. If Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code is properly analysed, then prima facie, we are of the view that Section 328 can be made applicable in view of the language used in the later part of the Section.
The applicant is running a business establishment and at the time of search of his business establishment, huge quantity of the contraband was seized.
Therefore, prima facie, the applicant is covered by the later part of the provisions of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code.

the Hon'ble Apex Court observed that it has not decided the powers of the High Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., but in the facts and circumstances of the case, it was observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the High Court ought not to have issued the direction that no coercive action should be taken against Naval Kishore and therefore, that part of the order passed by the Allahabad High Court was set aside.

Additionally, direction was given for issuance of notice and service on the appellant which has not been done by respondent no.1-accused.

The fact that the charge-sheet has been filed or bail has been granted is really of no consequence because of the fact that relief in the regular bail application appears to have been granted to respondent no.1 in view of the interim protection given by the High Court to the accused by the impugned order."

sentences.text: under Article 226 of the Constitution or Section 482 CrPC, it exercises judicial restraint.

We may hasten to clarify that the Court, if it thinks fit, regard being had to the parameters of quashing and the self-restraint imposed by law, has the jurisdiction to quash the investigation and may pass appropriate interim orders as thought apposite in law, but it is absolutely inconceivable and unthinkable to pass an order of the present nature while declining to interfere or expressing opinion that it is not appropriate to stay the investigation.
This kind of order is really inappropriate and unseemly.
It has no sanction in law.

The Courts should oust and obstruct unscrupulous litigants from invoking the inherent jurisdiction of the Court on the drop of a hat to file an application for quashing of launching an FIR or investigation and then seek relief by an interim order.

It is the obligation of the court to keep such unprincipled and unethical litigants at bay."
24.
Also there is one case of the Hon'ble Apex Court between Hamida and Rashid alisa Rasheed and others , reported in (2008) 1 SCC 474.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the complainant 13 141220apl800.20.odt approached to the Hon'ble Apex Court challenging the judgment and order of the Allahabad High Court, by which the petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. filed by the respondent/ accused was disposed of with certain directions.

By the impugned order, it was directed that the respondent/accused who was finally granted bail in an offence under Sections 324, 353 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Muzaffarnagar, would continue to remain on bail even after the offence had been converted to one under Section 304 of Indian Penal Code, if they furnished the requisite personal bonds and sureties before the Court concerned.

In this backdrop, the Hon'ble Apex Court in paragraph 10, ruled as under :
"10.
In the case in hand, the respondents- accused could apply for bail afresh after the offence had been converted into one under Section 304 IPC.

They deliberately did not do so and filed a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. in order to circumvent the procedure whereunder they would have been required to surrender as the bail application could be entertained and heard only if the accused were in custody.
It is important to note that no order adverse to the accused respondents had been passed by any Court nor there was any miscarriage of justice or any illegality.

In such circumstances, the High Court committed manifest error of law in entertaining a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and issuing a direction to the subordinate court to accept the sureties and bail bonds for the offence under Section 304 IPC.

The effect of the order passed by the High Court is that the accused after getting bail in an offence under Section 324, 352 and 506 IPC on the very day on 14 141220apl800.20.odt which they were taken into custody, got an order of bail in their favour even after the injured had succumbed to his injuries and the case had been converted into one under Section 304 IPC without any Court examining the case on merits, as it stood after conversion of the offence.

The procedure laid down for grant of bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., though available to the accused respondents, having not been availed of, the exercise of power by the High Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is clearly illegal and the impugned order passed by it has to be set aside.

25. sentences.text:
This attempt on the part of the applicant is impermissible and the mandate of the Hon'ble Apex Court is that the High Court shall not allow conversion of the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. into one under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
26.
In addition to the aforesaid, here, the applicant has firstly invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.

His application was not only rejected by the learned Single Judge, but in paragraph 12, which is reproduced in the body of this order, this Court after perusing the material placed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor has observed that the custodial interrogation of the applicant is 15 141220apl800.20.odt necessary in the interest of just and effective investigation.

27. Though, the powers of this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. are wide enough,
however at the same time, this Court while exercising the same, cannot seat as an Appellate Court over the order passed by the learned Single Judge, who exercised the powers under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
28.
The applicant, if was aggrieved by the rejection of his pre-arrest bail, it was and is well open for him to approach the Hon'ble Apex Court by challenging the order of rejection of anticipatory bail.

However, since this Court is not an Appellate Court and when there are specific observations by the learned Single Judge that custodial presence of the applicant is necessary, the applicant cannot be permitted to use the provisions of Section 482 of Cr.P.C. as a tool to circumvent the procedure and claim the relief, which is already rejected by this Court while dismissing his application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
29.

Since, the case of the applicant is covered by the later part of the language of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code, at least prima facie, an impediment cannot be created for the Investigating Officer to investigate into the crime.

If the prayer made by the learned senior Advocate is granted, it will amount to stalling the investigation,
which is a right of the Investigating Officer to investigate into the matter, especially when, prima facie, the material is available on record that the applicant has committed the offence for which the crime is registered against him.

In totality of the circumstances, we are 16 141220apl800.20.odt rejecting the interim prayer of stay of investigation in Crime No. 325/2020, registered with Police Station, Imamwada,
Nagpur and also reject the prayer made by the learned senior Advocate that during pendency of the present application, no coercive steps should be taken against the applicant and/or there shall not be arrest of the applicant in the said crime.

30. Since, we have issued notice qua Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code only, at this stage, we are not making any comment in respect of applicability of the decision in Nilesh Narayan Sanghavi .vs. State of Maharashtra, in Criminal Application (APL)

The failure of the High Court to do so has led it to adopting a position where it left the appellant to pursue his remedies for regular bail under Section 439.
Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is for grant of pre-arrest bail while, jurisdiction of the High Court is invoked under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of the FIR or charge-sheet, and the scope of these two provisions contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure is different.
After the seizure, a crime was registered at Police Station,
Imamwada, Nagpur vide Crime No. 325/2020 for the offence punishable under Sections 26, 27 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code.
15. If Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code is properly analysed, then prima facie, we are of the view that Section 328 can be made applicable in view of the language used in the later part of the Section.
The applicant is running a business establishment and at the time of search of his business establishment, huge quantity of the contraband was seized.
Therefore, prima facie, the applicant is covered by the later part of the provisions of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code.
18. After rejection of the application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for pre-arrest bail by this Court on 01.12.2020, the applicant has invoked the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. by filing present application on 07.12.2020.
19.
Whether the Court while exercising power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. can convert the said application into an application for pre-arrest bail is decided by the Hon'ble Apex Court in view of the various authoritative pronouncements.
In our view, the High Court, while deciding the petition filed under Section 482 of the Code by the respondent, ought not to have directed the authority that no adverse or punitive action be taken against the petitioner and in fact this was wholly unnecessary for the disposal of the criminal case.
27. Though, the powers of this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. are wide enough,
however at the same time, this Court while exercising the same, cannot seat as an Appellate Court over the order passed by the learned Single Judge, who exercised the powers under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
28.
The applicant, if was aggrieved by the rejection of his pre-arrest bail, it was and is well open for him to approach the Hon'ble Apex Court by challenging the order of rejection of anticipatory bail.
However, since this Court is not an Appellate Court and when there are specific observations by the learned Single Judge that custodial presence of the applicant is necessary, the applicant cannot be permitted to use the provisions of Section 482 of Cr.P.C. as a tool to circumvent the procedure and claim the relief, which is already rejected by this Court while dismissing his application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
29.
Since, the case of the applicant is covered by the later part of the language of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code, at least prima facie, an impediment cannot be created for the Investigating Officer to investigate into the crime.
If the prayer made by the learned senior Advocate is granted, it will amount to stalling the investigation,
which is a right of the Investigating Officer to investigate into the matter, especially when, prima facie, the material is available on record that the applicant has committed the offence for which the crime is registered against him.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The appeal is disposed of.
The order passed by the High Court "that no adverse or punitive action be taken against the petitioner in pursuance of FIR No.110/2004 till the instant petition is decided" is deleted."
21.
In totality of the circumstances, we are 16 141220apl800.20.odt rejecting the interim prayer of stay of investigation in Crime No. 325/2020, registered with Police Station, Imamwada,
Nagpur and also reject the prayer made by the learned senior Advocate that during pendency of the present application, no coercive steps should be taken against the applicant and/or there shall not be arrest of the applicant in the said crime.
30. Since, we have issued notice qua Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code only, at this stage, we are not making any comment in respect of applicability of the decision in Nilesh Narayan Sanghavi .vs. State of Maharashtra, in Criminal Application (APL)
Needless to mention that the observations made in this order are restricted only for refusing the interim relief.
